clue.text: Earnings of a sergeant, perhaps, in one northern state

indicators.note: in places the sergeant's letters between the two pieces that follow it

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
ME is the postal abbreviation for Maine, in the far north-east of the USA
a sergeant is an example of a non-commissioned officer, abbreviated NCO

explanation.surface: A sergeant's pay in a state up north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like a condition but is an American one, Maine; 'in' is the container signal and 'of' only joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: what you earn in wages or salary is the money coming in.

clue.text: Compelling little sibling to be put in goal

indicators.note: to be put in tells us the sibling goes inside the word for goal

parts.note: an intent is an aim or goal
sis is the short (little) form of sister, a sibling

explanation.surface: Forcing a younger brother or sister to play goalkeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' signals a shortened word, not a small child, and 'goal' is an aim, not a football net; 'to be put in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a demand that is pressing and will not be refused.

clue.text: Bottle' manufactured centuries before the present era

indicators.note: before places the abbreviation ahead of the phrase for the present era

parts.note: C is an abbreviation for century or centuries, as in 19th c.
the era we live in is 'our age'

explanation.surface: A glass vessel made hundreds of years BC.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' is British slang for nerve or bravery. 'before' puts C ahead of OUR AGE; the surface suggests a date BC.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang: to have bottle is to have nerve or bravery.

clue.text: Scottish beauty queen trains to be an evangelist

parts.note: beauty queens are titled Miss plus a place; Iona is a Scottish island, so whimsically Miss Iona
RY is the abbreviation for railway, i.e. trains

explanation.surface: A pageant winner from Scotland studies to become a preacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trains' looks like a verb but is the railway, RY. Iona is an island in the Inner Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: someone sent out to spread the gospel and convert others.

clue.text: Bad step taken behind the scenes

parts.note: food that has gone bad is off
a stage is a step in a process

explanation.surface: A wrong move made out of public view.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre sense: in the wings, out of the audience's sight.

clue.text: Assemble at Hindhead in Smith's place? Right

indicators.note: in tells us the letters before it sit inside the smith's workplace

parts.note: a blacksmith works in a forge
taken as written
read as 'Hind head', the head (first letter) of the word Hind

explanation.surface: Meet up at Hindhead, at the Smiths' house? Correct.
explanation.walkthrough: Hindhead is a Surrey village, but must be read as 'Hind head', the first letter of Hind. 'Smith's' is the trade, not a surname; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to come together or gather in one place.

clue.text: Some wish Iphigenia had used this transport

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Thoughts on how a Greek princess ought to have travelled.
explanation.walkthrough: In myth Iphigenia was sacrificed so that the Greek fleet could sail for Troy, which gives the surface its point.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a vessel is one means of travel she might have taken.

clue.text: Old man once about to go round Channel Islands

indicators.note: to go round tells us the word for about wraps the islands' abbreviation

parts.note: anent is an old and Scottish word meaning about or concerning
CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands, off the French coast

explanation.surface: An elderly fellow used to be on the point of touring Jersey and Guernsey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks the noun sense, an aged man, as archaic, so 'man' belongs to the definition. 'about' is not a reversal or container signal here; 'to go round' is.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic noun sense: an aged person or elder.

clue.text: Mistake made in eliminating source of intimidation

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter, and eliminating says that letter is struck off

parts.note: terror is fear used to intimidate

explanation.surface: A blunder committed while getting rid of whoever was making threats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eliminating source of' removes the first letter, T, from TERROR. 'made in' links definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a slip or blunder.

clue.text: Admiral sounds like a crooner

indicators.note: sounds like tells us the singer's name is heard, not spelt, to give the answer

parts.note: Bing Crosby was the best-known crooner of the twentieth century

explanation.surface: A naval commander has the voice of a smooth singer.
explanation.walkthrough: Admiral John Byng was a British naval officer shot in 1757 for failing to relieve Minorca.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the surname of an eighteenth-century British naval commander.

clue.text: Game has youth leader feeling like pulp

parts.note: squash is a racket game played in a walled court

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front

explanation.surface: A match leaves the scout master feeling beaten to a pulp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes the first letter of 'youth'. 'has' simply joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: soft and mushy to the touch.

clue.text: Upset about being carried in Republicans' coach

indicators.note: being carried in says the first two pieces travel inside the Republicans' letters

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican, so two of them give RR
to ail someone is to trouble or upset them
CA is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: Someone distressed at being a passenger on the Republicans' bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' is a verb here, to trouble, not an anagram or reversal signal; 'being carried in' is the container signal and 'about' is circa.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a self-propelled railway carriage.

clue.text: South London borough, say, beats this for security

parts.note: Ealing is a borough in west London

indicators.note: say tells us the word for beats is spoken, not written

parts.note: whacks means hits or beats

explanation.surface: A south London district outdoes this one for safety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives WAX from the sound of WHACKS. It was melted and stamped to close letters and documents against tampering.
explanation.definitionFit: Use: melted and stamped on a letter so that tampering shows.

clue.text: He succeeds in belonging to them, though not at first

indicators.note: though not at first says the opening letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: their means belonging to them

explanation.surface: A man eventually manages to become one of the group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'though not at first' drops the opening T of THEIR. 'succeeds' means inherits, not triumphs.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the person who inherits a title or estate.

clue.text: Irritation caused by revision of the rentals

indicators.note: a revision is a reworking, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Annoyance after the letting charges were changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revision of' rearranges THE RENTALS. The irritation is literal: an itchy skin eruption, also called hives.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an itchy skin eruption, also called hives.

clue.text: Unidentified person left outside? It's always so

indicators.note: left says the unidentified person has departed from the word for outside

parts.note: external means outside
X stands for an unnamed person, as in Mr X

explanation.surface: A stranger is kept out in the cold, as ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' is the verb departed: X leaves EXTERNAL. It is not the direction L.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraphrase: lasting for ever, without end.

clue.text: It illuminates an innocent creature's endless predicament

indicators.note: endless says the creature loses its last letter

parts.note: a lamb is the proverbial innocent creature
a plight is a difficult situation

explanation.surface: It sheds light on a blameless animal's never-ending trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' applies to the innocent creature before it, which loses its last letter, not to the predicament that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the glow from an oil or electric lantern.

clue.text: Lean over to drain what's left at bottom of glass.

definitions.text: what's left at bottom of glass

parts.note: a ship that heels leans over to one side
to tap a cask or a tree is to draw liquid off from it

explanation.surface: Tipping a tumbler to finish the last drops.
explanation.definitionFit: Dictionary sense: the dregs of drink remaining after someone has drunk.

clue.text: A payment made to go into an attendant's ancestry

indicators.note: made to go into says the first two pieces are placed inside the attendant

parts.note: a page is a boy attendant
rent is a regular payment to a landlord

explanation.surface: Money paid for research into a servant's family tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: one's descent or lineage.

clue.text: Article could be more a proposition

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: could be says the letters before it might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece might amount to something of an offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges MORE into OREM. 'Article' is grammar, not journalism.
explanation.definitionFit: Mathematical sense: a statement to be proved.

clue.text: Fellow supporting point-to-point is a public school type

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath the other

parts.note: two compass points joined by 'to': E to N
Ian is a man's name

explanation.surface: A chap backing the amateur horse races went to a posh school.
explanation.walkthrough: A point-to-point is a British amateur steeplechase; here it is compass points, E to N. 'supporting' puts IAN beneath in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a pupil of a famous English fee-paying boys' college near Windsor.

clue.text: Reptile found by terrier crossing lake

indicators.note: crossing says the dog's letters go across the lake's abbreviation

parts.note: a terrier bred to catch rats is a ratter
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A dog swimming across the water comes upon a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' puts L inside RATTER; 'found by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal name for a venomous American snake with a noisy tail.

clue.text: The French island bound to be used for relaxation

parts.note: le is 'the' in French
I is the map abbreviation for island
bound to happen means sure to happen

explanation.surface: An isle off France is certain to become a holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' means certain here, not tied or leaping. 'to be used for' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: free time spent at ease.

clue.text: A small bird in the wood

definitions.meaning: a small wading bird of the sandpiper family seen on British shores
a hard round lump found in timber where a branch once grew

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a sandpiper-like wader, and a hard lump in timber where a branch grew.

clue.text: Food upset the infant Kelvin

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means overturned, so the pieces after it read upwards

parts.note: a babe is an infant
K is the symbol for the kelvin, the unit of temperature

explanation.surface: Something he ate disagreed with baby Kelvin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' overturns the whole run BABE K, read from the bottom up in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: grilled meat on a skewer.

clue.text: Scottish city gal sewing a shift?

definitions.text: Scottish city gal sewing a shift?

indicators.note: to shift letters is to move them about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl from a town in Scotland stitching a simple dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' is a dress in the surface but tells the letters of GAL SEWING A to move. The whole clue describes one such citizen.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a girl from Scotland's largest town on the Clyde would be one.

clue.text: Military band?

parts.note: a band here is a strip of cloth worn across the shoulder or round the waist of a uniform, not a group of musicians

explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: officers wear this strip of cloth as part of dress uniform.

clue.text: Operatic heroine in Rhodes, say?

indicators.note: say tells us the island's name is to be heard as another word

parts.note: Rhodes is pronounced like roads; two British roads are the M1 and the M1 again, the figure 1 written as I

explanation.surface: A soprano's leading role on a Greek island, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns Rhodes into roads, and the M1 is Britain's first motorway: two of them, with 1 written as I. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the seamstress in Puccini's La Boheme.

clue.text: Right to abandon another cooking method for this

indicators.note: to abandon says the letter for right walks out of the cooking word

parts.note: broiling is cooking by direct heat, grilling

explanation.surface: It is sensible to give up one way of preparing food in favour of this one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to abandon' has R leave BROILING. 'another' tells us the answer is itself a way of cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: cooking in bubbling water is one such way of preparing food.

clue.text: Break up salt with a kitchen utensil

indicators.note: to break something is to smash it into pieces, so the letters after it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Crush the lumps of salt using a cooking tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break' rearranges UP SALT into SPATUL; 'up' is fodder, not part of the signal. 'with' adds the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a flat-bladed tool for lifting and spreading.

clue.text: In part also it backed gangsters

indicators.note: In says the word for also sits inside the word for part

parts.note: a bit is a small part
and means also

indicators.note: backed says the word before it is written back to front

explanation.surface: To some extent, the film It was also funded by mobsters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is used twice over in spirit: the first comes free from the container that 'In' makes, and only the printed 'it' is turned by 'backed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian plural: outlaws or brigands operating in gangs.

clue.text: A person of importance in Cheshire, for instance

definitions.meaning: slang for a bigwig, usually with 'big' in front
Cheshire is an English county that gives its name to a crumbly dairy product

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: slang for a bigwig, and the dairy food of which the English county's crumbly variety is one.
